data.name: Nabab
data.gender_notes: Nabab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Lord of the night, God of the new moon
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit term ‘Nabhah’ meaning ‘sky’ or ‘heavens’, the name Nabab is a revered title given to the Hindu god of the night, Chandra, or the moon god. Nabab is also known as the god of the new moon and is considered a symbol of creation, regeneration, and new beginnings. The name Nabab carries the meaning “Lord of the night, God of the new moon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nabab usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the night, god of the new moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the cycle of creation and destruction, and the infinite potential for renewal and transformation.
data.etymology: Nabab belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the night, God of the new moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nabab total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_significance: Nabab, as a spiritual manifestation, represents the constant cycle of creation, destruction, and rebirth. It evokes feelings of peace, tranquility, and introspection, inspiring individuals to seek inner wisdom and enlightenment.
